title: Integer base encode/decode round trip
description: Implement to_base(number, base) and from_base(text, base) for bases 2 through 36 with digits '0'-'9' then 'a'-'z' (digit value 10..35). to_base(number, base): number must be an int that is not a bool (else TypeError) and must be >= 0 (else ValueError); returns the canonical lowercase representation with no leading zeros, so to_base(0, b) == '0' and to_base(255, 16) == 'ff'. from_base(text, base): text must be a str (else TypeError); it is stripped of surrounding whitespace and matched case-insensitively; the remaining string must be non-empty and contain only digits valid for the base (each digit's value must be < base), else ValueError; leading zeros are accepted ('007' -> 7); '+'/'-' signs are not accepted. base must be an int that is not a bool (else TypeError) in the range 2..36 inclusive (else ValueError) for both functions.
invariants: Round trip: from_base(to_base(n, b), b) == n for every int n >= 0 and every base b in 2..36.
Canonical output: to_base never emits leading zeros (except the single '0' for zero) and always uses lowercase letters.
from_base accepts surrounding whitespace, mixed case, and leading zeros; it rejects empty/blank strings, signs, and any digit whose value >= base ('2' in base 2, 'z' in base 35).
base is validated identically in both functions: non-int or bool is TypeError, outside 2..36 is ValueError.
bool numbers are TypeError even though bool subclasses int; float and str numbers are TypeError too.
Digit 'z' (value 35) is valid only in base 36.
